html:
Zululand is the land of the Zulu kingdom north of the Tugela River, in what is now KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900, the years after Britain broke the kingdom's power.

In 1879 Britain invaded. The Zulu army won a famous victory at Isandlwana, but lost the Anglo-Zulu War at Ulundi that July. King Cetshwayo was captured, and the British split the kingdom among thirteen chiefs, which led to civil war.

Cetshwayo was allowed back to rule part of the land in 1883, but was defeated by a rival chief and died in 1884. His son Dinuzulu won back power with the help of Boer volunteers, who took a large part of the land as their reward. Britain annexed what was left in 1887, exiled Dinuzulu after a revolt, and in 1897 handed Zululand to Natal.
